# dsh-markboard · conversation marks for DSH
中文 | English
A **conversation markboard** for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web UI: turn any conversation turn into
a named task card, jump straight back to it later, or quote its answer into the composer and keep wo
rking. Marks live in your browser.
> Stop scrolling through history to find "that conclusion from earlier". Mark it once, then pick fro
m a handful of rows.
## Screenshots
| Mark action on each turn + header count | The markboard in the right Sidebar |
| Fill the composer from a card | Jump back to the turn |
## Features
- **Mark a whole turn** — a Mark action under every completed answer records the turn (your prompt p

lus this turn's answer) and names it from the prompt's first sentence. Click again to remove it.
- *

*Header count** — the Session header shows how many turns are marked; click it to open the board.
-
**Right-Sidebar page** — its own tab beside Files and Browser, with "this session" / "all sessions"

scopes and search over labels, content, and turn numbers.
- **Rename and delete** — click a card's t

itle to rename it; deletion comes with an undo.
- **Jump back** — opens the owning session and scrol
ls the turn into view. When that turn is outside the loaded window, history is paged in first throug

h the kernel's exact `loadThrough(seq)`, and the landing row flashes once.
- **Fill the composer** —
writes the turn's answer into the current draft as a plain-text quote (`> 标记 · session · turn N`) t
hat you can keep editing or delete; the previous draft is restorable. A card from another session fi
lls the composer you are already typing in, without switching sessions, and appends after any existi

ng draft instead of replacing it.
- **Cross-tab sync** — another tab of the same origin writing mark

s updates this one.
- **Bilingual** copy that follows the interface language.

## Usage

1. Find the turn you want to keep and click **Mark** in the action row under the answer.
2. The head

er shows a count; click it (or press `Ctrl+Alt+M`) to open the markboard.
3. Each card offers **Jump
** (back to the turn), **Fill composer** (quote the answer into the draft), and **Delete** (undoable

).
4. Click a card's title to rename it — the label is your task name.
## Shortcut
`Ctrl+Alt+M` (`⌘+Alt+M` on macOS) toggles the board. The binding is editable under Settings → Shortc
l+Alt+M` (`⌘+Alt+M` on macOS) toggles the board. The binding is editable under Settings → Shortcuts.
## How it works
Two halves, like any DSH surface plugin:
- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`): an empty `apply`. It only makes the package an ordinary Loader ent
ry, which is what lets `client-modules` discover the `dsh.client` declaration in `package.json` and

compose the browser half into `window.__DSH_BOOT__`.
- **Browser half** (`src/client`, built to `lib
/client.js`): registers three existing extension seats plus a `ctx.markboard` service.
| Place | Seat | What it adds |

| Turn action row | `conversation.chat.turnTail` | the Mark / Marked button |
| Session header | `co

nversation.session.header.utilities` | the mark count entry |
| Right Sidebar | `ctx.sidebarRightTab

s` + `sidebar.right.pane.tab` | the markboard page |
| Notices | `shell.overlay` | mark / fill / del
ete toasts with undo |
The data model is pure functions (`src/shared/marks.ts`); `sessionId + turn` is the identity, so mar
king the same turn twice edits that card instead of adding a second one. Marks persist in `localStor
age['dsh-markboard.v1']`. A failed write (quota, private mode) only reports — it never throws, and t
he in-memory list keeps working.
**Why not Host storage**: a personal board does not need cross-device sync, and the cost of localSto
rage is only that a different browser or origin starts empty — which the panel says out loud.
**Why the fill is plain text**: `insertText` / `setDraft` are the kernel's public action face. A ric
h quote chip would need kernel support for reference fragments — a different order of change that wo
uld also drift across kernel upgrades.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
End-to-end (**opens a real browser window** so you can watch the flow):

The script walks through: open a session → mark → open the panel → rename → fill the composer → jump
back → reload → search → delete and undo, writing one screenshot per stage to `docs/e2e/`. Add `--h
search → delete and undo, writing one screenshot per stage to `docs/e2e/`. Add `--headless` for CI.
## Known limitations
- **Turns only.** No per-message or text-selection marks; a per-sentence grain makes the card list u

nreadable fast.
- **Local to this browser.** No cross-browser or cross-origin sharing, and no export

.
- **Jumping depends on the turn's row existing**: a turn outside the loaded window triggers one ex

act history page-in first; if that fails the UI says so instead of failing silently.
- **The fill is

a plain-text quote** and does not carry the original message's attachments or images.
- **The page
is bound to a Session**: it follows session switches, and "all sessions" is a view inside the same p

age.
- **`Ctrl+Alt+M` only.** The shell's shortcut registry rejects a Web default that lacks the pla
tform primary on Linux, so the Linux Web profile stays unbound rather than registering a rejected ke
orm primary on Linux, so the Linux Web profile stays unbound rather than registering a rejected key.
